{{Infobox football match | title = 2025 Copa del Rey final | image = Estadioolimpicosevilla.jpg | alt = | event = [[2024–25 Copa del Rey]] | caption = [[Estadio de La Cartuja]] in [[Seville]] hosted the final. | team1 = [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] | team1score = 3 | team2 = [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] | team2score = 2 | details = After [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|extra time]] | date = {{Start date|2025|4|26|df=y}} | stadium = [[Estadio de La Cartuja|La Cartuja]] | city = [[Seville]] | man_of_the_match1a = [[Ferran Torres]] (Barcelona){{cite news |url=https://rfef.es/es/noticias/ferran-torres-mvp-de-la-finalisima |title=Ferran Torres, MVP de la finalísima |trans-title=Ferran Torres, MVP of the final |work=[[Royal Spanish Football Federation]] |date=26 April 2025|access-date=26 April 2025 |language=es}} | referee = [[Ricardo de Burgos Bengoetxea]]{{cite web |url=https://rfef.es/sites/default/files/utf-8designaciones_copa_sm_el_rey_final.pdf |title=Designación arbitral completa de la final de la Copa del Rey |trans-title=Complete referee appointment of the Copa del Rey final|publisher=[[Royal Spanish Football Federation]] |date=21 April 2025 |access-date=22 April 2025 |language=es}} | attendance = 55,579 | weather = | previous = [[2024 Copa del Rey final|2024]] | next = [[2026 Copa del Rey final|2026]] }} The '''2025 Copa del Rey final''' was a football match to decide the winners of the [[2024–25 Copa del Rey]], the 123rd edition of Spain's [[Copa del Rey|primary football cup]] (including two seasons where two rival editions were played). The match was played on 26 April 2025 at [[Estadio de La Cartuja]] in [[Seville]] – in the first event at the venue following its expansion and conversion from an athletics facility ahead of its use at the [[2030 FIFA World Cup]]{{cite web|url=https://as.com/futbol/copa_del_rey/adios-a-la-pista-de-atletismo-en-la-cartuja-esta-es-la-nueva-capacidad-que-tendra-el-estadio-de-la-final-de-copa-n/?id_externo_rsoc=CM_ES_TW|publisher=Diario AS|date=24 April 2025|title=Adiós a la pista de atletismo en La Cartuja: esta es la nueva capacidad que tendrá el estadio de la final de Copa|trans-title=Goodbye to the athletics track at La Cartuja: this is the new capacity of the Copa final stadium|language=es|access-date=27 April 2025}} – between [[El Clásico|arch rivals]] [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] and [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]].{{cite web|url=https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2025/4/2/barcelona-beat-atletico-to-set-up-real-madrid-final-in-copa-del-rey |publisher=aljazeera.com|title=Barcelona beat Atletico to set up Real Madrid final in Copa del Rey|date=2 April 2025|access-date=27 April 2025}} It was the 260th competitive match between the sides and the first in a Copa del Rey final since [[2014 Copa del Rey final|2014]]. Barcelona won the match 3–2 after [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|extra time]] for a record-extending 32nd Copa del Rey title.{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/apr/27/barcelona-real-madrid-copa-del-rey-match-report|title=Barcelona win thrilling Copa del Rey and drive Madrid to red card fury|date=27 April 2025|work=Guardian|accessdate=1 May 2025}} ==Route to the final== {{details|2024–25 Copa del Rey}} {| style="width:100%; (A) = Away {{reflist|group=lower-alpha}} ==Refereeing controversy== Ahead of the final, [[Real Madrid TV]] broadcast a video criticising the appointed match referee [[Ricardo de Burgos Bengoetxea]], stating that Barcelona won more often than Real Madrid in matches he refereed. RMTV disparaged De Burgos Bengoetxea for never being appointed to matches in the [[UEFA Champions League]] or [[FIFA]] tournaments, and included footage of several alleged refereeing errors against Real Madrid.{{cite web |url=https://www.goal.com/en/lists/video-real-madrid-tv-copa-del-rey-official-ricardo-de-burgos-bengoetxea-barcelona/blt334a3e8f98a739a3 |title=VIDEO: Real Madrid TV launch latest attack on Spanish referees by posting discouraging compilation of Copa del Rey official Ricardo de Burgos Bengoetxea ahead of final meeting with Barcelona |publisher=Goal.com |date=25 April 2025 }} De Burgos Bengoetxea responded at a press conference by highlighting difficulties faced by match officials and their families when their integrity is questioned, saying "When your child goes to school and is told their father is a thief by other kids, that's really tough".{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6309127/2025/04/26/real-madrid-barcelona-de-burgos-referee/ |title=Why a Spanish referee breaking down in tears caused a furious reaction from Real Madrid |publisher=The New York Times |date=26 April 2025 }} The final's [[video assistant referee]] Pablo González Fuertes suggested that Spanish match officials may take action such as a strike due to the way they were being treated.{{cite web |url=https://www.beinsports.com/en-asia/football/copa-del-rey/articles/real-madrid-deny-suggestions-they-could-boycott-copa-del-rey-final-2025-04-25?Lh=KQ |title=Real Madrid deny suggestions they could boycott Copa del Rey final |publisher=beIN SPORTS |date=26 April 2025 }} Real Madrid branded the officials' comments 'unacceptable' and withdrew from pre-final media duties, including the press Francisco José Hernández Maeso |style="width:60%; vertical-align:top;"| '''Match rules''' *90 minutes. *30 minutes of [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|extra time]] if necessary. *[[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|Penalty shoot-out]] if scores still level. *Eleven named substitutes. *Maximum of five substitutions, with a sixth allowed in extra time.{{refn|group=note|Each team was given only three opportunities to make substitutions, with a fourth opportunity in extra time, excluding substitutions made at half-time, before the start of extra time and at half-time in extra time.}} |} ==Aftermath== [[File:2025 04 26 Final de la Copa del Rey.jpg|thumb|[[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] lifting the trophy after winning the final against [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]].]] The match official [[Ricardo de Burgos Bengoetxea]] issued three red cards — all to [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] players. [[Antonio Rüdiger]], who had already been substituted, was shown a red card during the stoppage time of extra time for throwing an object toward the referee from the technical area. [[Lucas Vázquez]] was sent off for entering the pitch to protest a refereeing decision aggressively. After the final whistle, [[Jude Bellingham]] was also dismissed for confronting the referee in an aggressive manner and had to be restrained by teammates.{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6314786/2025/04/27/real-madrid-red-cards-copa-rudiger-bellingham-vazquez/ |title=Real Madrid’s red cards: Antonio Rudiger ‘threw object’ at referee, Jude Bellingham’s ‘aggressive behaviour’ |publisher=The New York Times |date=27 April 2025 }} After being sent off, Rüdiger publicly apologized for his behaviour, admitting there was no excuse for his actions and expressed regret for disappointing the fans.{{cite web |last=Skelton |first=Jack |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c9qw3dxjv9zo |title=Rudiger apologises for throwing object at referee |publisher=BBC Sport |date=27 April 2025 }} However, Rüdiger could be suspended for four to twelve matches, or up to three to six months if the offense is classified as more serious. Meanwhile, both Vázquez and Bellingham would receive two-match suspensions, which will be served in the [[2025–26 Copa del Rey|next season's Copa del Rey]].{{cite web |last=Corrigan |first=Dermot |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6304910/2025/04/27/real-madrid-barcelona-copa-final-rage/ |title=How 48 hours of rage and recrimination overshadowed the Copa del Rey final |publisher=The New York Times |date=27 April 2025 }} Ultimately, Rüdiger was handed a six-match ban across domestic competitions, while Bellingham's red card was rescinded and Vázquez received a two-match Copa del Rey suspension.{{cite web |last=Smith |first=Emma |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/ckge9rp8379o |title=Rudiger given six-game ban for throwing object at referee |publisher=BBC Sport |date=29 April 2025 }}{{cite web |last=Andrews |first=Connor |url=https://talksport.com/football/3162419/jude-bellingham-antonio-rudiger-ban-real-madrid-barcelona/?utm |title=Jude Bellingham exonerated as Antonio Rudiger discovers length of ban for Copa del Rey tantrum |publisher=talkSPORT |date=29 April 2025 }} ==Notes== {{reflist|group=note}} ==References== {{Reflist}} {{commons category}} {{Copa del Rey}} {{2024–25 in Spanish football}} {{FC Barcelona matches}} {{Real Madrid CF matches}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Copa del Rey final 2025}} [[Category:Copa del Rey finals|2025]] [[Category:Football competitions in Seville]] [[Category:2025 in Seville]] [[Category:2024–25 in Spanish football cups|1, final]] [[Category:April 2025 sports events in Spain|Copa del Rey]] [[Category:FC Barcelona matches]] [[Category:Real Madrid CF matches]] [[Category:El Clásico matches]] [[Category:2024–25 in Spanish men's football]]
